CONTEXT: Previous attempt created a separate "storefront-page" content type 
and a part, but hit issues: wrong content path resolution in the Next.js 
catch-all route (content lives at /home/[slug] but adapter only received 
[slug] as the path), and the page editor required manual part placement.

CORRECTED GOAL: Upgrade the EXISTING landing-page content type (don't create 
a new content type) to support real page composition, with a PAGE TEMPLATE 
that auto-populates sensible default content, which editors can then 
customize via Content Studio's visual page editor.

IMPORTANT CONTEXT (already confirmed via Enonic docs): there is no special 
"page-capable" superType — base:structured (what landing-page.yaml already 
uses) is fine as-is. Page assignment happens per-content-item via Content 
Studio's page editor and template system, not via schema changes. So:

STEPS:
1. Do NOT change landing-page.yaml's superType or add a regions section to 
   the content type schema itself.
2. Create a PAGE descriptor (cms/pages/landing/landing.yaml or similar) 
   with one or more named regions (e.g. "main"), following the pattern of 
   the existing cms/pages/main/main.yaml if one exists (check first).
3. Create the Product Showcase PART (cms/parts/product-showcase/) with a 
   CustomSelector config field reusing the existing working medusaProducts 
   service (same config pattern as collection.yaml's featuredProducts field: 
   config: { service: "medusaProducts" }), plus a heading TextLine field.
4. Create a PAGE TEMPLATE (portal:page-template content, or via 
   import/hmdb-style XML/node definition if that's how templates are 
   provisioned in this app) that uses the landing page descriptor and has 
   the Product Showcase part PRE-PLACED in the main region with sensible 
   default config, so any new Landing Page automatically starts populated, 
   not blank.
5. Update site.yaml's mappings so the landing-page content type renders via 
   this page descriptor/template (replacing the previous storefront-page 
   mapping entry if one was added).
6. Remove the previous storefront-page content type and its mapping entry 
   from site.yaml if they were created in the last session — confirm with 
   me before deleting if any real content exists under that type.

FRONTEND FIX:
7. The Next.js catch-all route at frontend/src/app/[countryCode]/[...contentPath]/
   page.tsx already exists and uses the adapter's fetchContent/MainView 
   pattern. The bug found: a Landing Page content item at path /home/summer-launch 
   only resolves correctly at URL /dk/home/summer-launch, NOT /dk/summer-launch 
   — this is just because the content lives nested under /home. This is 
   expected/correct behavior given XP's content tree, not a bug to fix in 
   code. Just confirm this route correctly renders content at whatever 
   nested path it actually lives at.
8. Map the "product-showcase" part name in the adapter's ComponentRegistry 
   (frontend/src/components/_mappings.ts) to a new React component that 
   fetches the selected products from Medusa (via existing 
   src/lib/data/products.ts) and renders them.

VERIFY: Create a brand new Landing Page in Content Studio (don't reuse 
"Summer Launch" if it was made under the old broken setup) — it should 
appear with the Product Showcase part already placed and showing default/
placeholder content immediately, with the option to edit which products 
are selected. Confirm it renders correctly at its real nested URL on the 
Next.js frontend.

Do not break: /dk homepage, /dk/products, /dk/products/[handle], 
/dk/collections/[handle], /dk/Blog/[slug].

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- medusa-dev:building-admin-dashboard-customizations: Load automatically when planning, researching, or implementing Medusa Admin dashboard UI (widgets, custom pages, forms, tables, data loading, navigation). REQUIRED for all admin UI work in ALL modes (planning, implementation, exploration). Contains design patterns, component usage, and data loading patterns that MCP servers don't provide.
- medusa-dev:building-storefronts: Load automatically when planning, researching, or implementing Medusa storefront features (calling custom API routes, SDK integration, React Query patterns, data fetching). REQUIRED for all storefront development in ALL modes (planning, implementation, exploration). Contains SDK usage patterns, frontend integration, and critical rules for calling Medusa APIs.
- medusa-dev:building-with-medusa: Load automatically when planning, researching, or implementing ANY Medusa backend features (custom modules, API routes, workflows, data models, module links, business logic). REQUIRED for all Medusa backend work in ALL modes (planning, implementation, exploration). Contains architectural patterns, best practices, and critical rules that MCP servers don't provide.
- medusa-dev:creating-internal-agents: Use when building an internal admin-facing AI agent in a Medusa project. These agents are operated by merchants and store operators — not customers. Covers data models, module service, agent runtime (tools, system prompt, streamText), streaming API routes (NDJSON), and admin UI chat extensions. Load for any internal agent type: store operations assistant, product audit, cohort analysis, customer service tooling for support staff, etc. Do NOT use for customer-facing agents (storefront chatbots, buyer-side assistants).
- medusa-dev:db-generate: Generate database migrations for a Medusa module
- medusa-dev:db-migrate: Run database migrations in Medusa
- medusa-dev:new-user: Create an admin user in Medusa
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

description: Architecture and key facts about the Instant Storefront project (Enonic XP8 + Next.js 15 + Medusa)

  node_type: memory
  type: project

---

# Instant Storefront — project facts

Stack: enonic-app (com.enonic.app.hmdb, XP8) + frontend (Next.js 15 App Router) + medusa-backend (:9000).

**Content Studio / Enonic**
- Sandbox name: `typescript` (running on :8080)
- CMS project: `hmdb`, repo: `com.enonic.cms.hmdb`
- Template folder is at `/home/_templates` (NOT `/hmdb/_templates`) — this sandbox has a custom content structure where the site root is `/home`, not `/hmdb`. The import data creates content under `/hmdb/` but on this sandbox the site was set up differently.
- medusaProducts custom selector service: `services/medusaProducts/` (kind: Service, requires `allow: role:system.everyone`)
- In CustomSelector YAML, use bare service name `medusaProducts` (no app prefix)

**Page composition feature (added 2026-06-25)**
- New content type: `cms/content-types/storefront-page/storefront-page.yaml`
- New part: `cms/parts/product-showcase/product-showcase.yaml` + `.ts` (controller)
- Page controller: `cms/pages/main/main.ts` — renders page canvas with `data-portal-region="main"`
- site.yaml: added mapping `com.enonic.app.hmdb:storefront-page` → `/cms/pages/main/main.js`
- Template creation: `main.ts` `ensureStorefrontPageTemplate()` uses dynamic query to find template folder (don't hardcode `/hmdb/_templates`)
- Import data template: `import/hmdb/_templates/storefront-page/_/node.xml` (for fresh installs)

**Frontend (Next.js)**
- Enonic adapter route: `src/app/[countryCode]/[...contentPath]/page.tsx` — uses `fetchContent` + `MainView`
- ENONIC_MAPPINGS: `en:hmdb,dk:hmdb` (both locales map to the hmdb site)
- New components: `src/components/enonic/pages/MainPage.tsx`, `src/components/enonic/parts/ProductShowcase.tsx`
- Registered in `src/components/_mappings.ts` via `ComponentRegistry.addPage/addPart`
- `Part_com_enonic_app_hmdb_product_showcase` config arrives in `part.config` as `{ heading?, products? }` (adapter extracts from `configAsJson`)
- TS error `moduleResolution: "node"` for adapter imports is pre-existing and suppressed by `typescript: { ignoreBuildErrors: true }` in next.config.js

**Why:** enonic/fix-page-templates.ts uses `/home/collection`, `/home/t-shirt` — confirms the live sandbox has content under `/home/` not `/hmdb/`
**How to apply:** When writing `contentLib` queries against this sandbox, use dynamic `contentLib.query()` to find paths rather than hardcoding `/hmdb/...`

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project

Headless Movie DB (hmdb) — an Enonic XP sample/demonstration application (`com.enonic.app.hmdb`) that ships sample movie content and renders simple preview pages. Targets XP `8.0.0-SNAPSHOT` (see `gradle.properties`). Not a library/API-only app: it registers a site with controllers and content types, and auto-imports sample data on first install.

## Build & deploy

XP apps compile **through the connected sandbox**, not via the host JDK/Gradle. The Enonic CLI picks the sandbox from the `.enonic` file (gitignored) and the sandbox provides the JDK + Gradle runtime used for the build — don't debug build errors by inspecting local `java -version` or running `./gradlew` directly, and don't assume the host's Java matches what the build uses.

Primary commands:
- `enonic project build` — compile the app inside the connected sandbox.
- `enonic project deploy` — build and deploy the jar to the sandbox.
- `enonic project sandbox` — re-associate or switch the connected sandbox.

The `build.gradle` / `settings.gradle` files are authoritative for dependencies and plugins (`com.enonic.xp.app`, `com.enonic.xp.settings` from `settings.gradle`, and the `xplibs.*` version catalog), but the wrapper is invoked by the CLI against the sandbox runtime, so versions here must be compatible with what the sandbox ships — don't pin library versions inline; always go through `xplibs.*`.

The server code is **TypeScript**, compiled to `build/resources/main` by `tsdown` (config: `tsdown.config.ts`, one output `.js` per source file with the tree intact). Gradle drives npm via the `com.github.node-gradle.node` plugin: `npmBuild` (→ `jar`) runs `npm run build`, and `npmCheck` (→ `check`) runs `tsc --noEmit` + ESLint. `processResources` excludes `*.ts`/`*.tsx`/`*.json`/`.gitkeep` so only the compiled `.js` plus the copied descriptors land in the jar. You can run the toolchain directly (no sandbox needed) from the repo root: `npm install`, then `npm run check` / `npm run build`.

Type definitions come from `@enonic-types/*` (dev-only); `/lib/thymeleaf` types come from `@item-enonic-types/lib-thymeleaf`. No test framework is currently wired. The CI workflow (`.github/workflows/enonic-gradle.yml`) runs the shared `enonic/release-tools/build-and-publish` action.

## First-boot bootstrapping

`src/main/resources/main.ts` is the application entry point. On the cluster leader (`clusterLib.isLeader()`) it:

1. Runs in an admin context on repo `com.enonic.cms.hmdb`.
2. If the `hmdb` project does not exist, creates it via `lib-project` (`publicRead: true`, language `en`).
3. Imports `/import/hmdb` into `/content` using `exportLib.importNodes`, applying `import/replace_app.xsl` with `applicationId=app.name` so the exported XML references to the old app name are rewritten to the currently-deployed app on import.
4. Publishes `/hmdb` to `master`. In XP8 `contentLib.publish` takes no source/target branch — it publishes from the current context branch (`draft`, set in `runInContext`) to `master`, descendants included by default.

If you change `appName` in `gradle.properties` the XSLT substitution is what keeps imported content referring to the right app. Don't bypass it by hardcoding app IDs in the exported data.

## Resource layout (XP8)

Under `src/main/resources/`:

- `application.yaml` — top-level app manifest (`kind: "Application"`, title, description, vendor).
- `cms/` — all schemas the CMS cares about:
  - `site.yaml` — portal mappings (controllers matched by content type) and mounted Universal APIs (`apis:`, e.g. `asset`).
  - `cms.yaml` — app-level mixin bindings (which content types get which mixin fields).
  - `content-types/`, `pages/`, `parts/`, `layouts/`, `macros/`, `mixins/`, `styles/` — all YAML descriptors.
- `main.ts` — application entry point (see First-boot bootstrapping).
- `lib/` — portal controllers (TypeScript) registered via `cms/site.yaml` mappings:
  - `info.ts` — matches `type:'portal:site'`, plain HTML landing page.
  - `preview.ts` — matches `type:'(?!media:).*'` (every non-media type), uses `lib-thymeleaf` to render `preview.html` (a copied resource, not compiled).
- `i18n/` — translation bundles (`phrases.properties`, `phrases_no.properties`). Must live at `/i18n/`, not `/site/i18n/` (XP8 removed the site-scoped lookup).
- `assets/` — static assets (including `styles.css`). Served by `lib-asset`'s bundled **Asset API** (`assetUrl` is imported from `/lib/enonic/asset`, not `/lib/xp/portal`). The API ships inside the `lib-asset` jar; the app mounts it by listing `asset` under `apis:` in `cms/site.yaml` (XP8 Universal APIs are not exposed by default).
- `import/hmdb/` — XP content export used for first-boot bootstrapping, with `replace_app.xsl` rewriting app IDs on import.

Controllers are authored in TypeScript and compiled to `.js`, so the controller names in `cms/site.yaml` (e.g. `/lib/info.js`) are the **compiled** output paths. Use named uppercase HTTP-method exports — `export function GET(req)` / `POST` (compiled to `exports.GET`) — XP8 deprecated lowercase method names. A lowercase `all` export stays lowercase.

## Samples (not built)

`samples/review/` contains an example `review` content type XML and is **not** under `src/` — it's a copy-paste example for consumers of this demo, not part of the build. Leave it as a sample unless the user explicitly asks.

## Working conventions specific to XP apps

- Resources under `src/main/resources/` are served as classpath resources by XP; the `/lib/...` paths in controller `import` statements (and `resolve('...')` calls) are classpath-relative, not filesystem-relative. tsdown compiles the ESM `import`s to CommonJS and keeps the `/lib/xp/*` + `/lib/thymeleaf` references external (provided by the platform at runtime).
- Library deps in `build.gradle` use the `xplibs.*` catalog (e.g. `include xplibs.content`), not version-pinned coordinates. Third-party libs like `lib-thymeleaf` still use explicit coordinates.
- `include` vs `implementation` in `build.gradle`: `include` bundles the library inside the deployed app jar (used for `lib-xp:*` runtime libs and third-party `lib-*` deps), `implementation` is a compile-time-only XP API (e.g. `xplibs.api.script`). Keep that distinction when adding dependencies.
- Mixin bindings are split: mixin schemas live in `cms/mixins/<name>/<name>.yaml`, and the binding of "which content types get this mixin" lives in `cms/cms.yaml` under `mixins:` (with an `allowContentTypes` regex). Site mappings live separately in `cms/site.yaml`.

1	<?xml version="1.0"?>
2	<xsl:stylesheet version="1.0" xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform">
3	  <xsl:output method="xml" indent="yes"/>
4	
5	  <xsl:param name="applicationId"/>
6	  <xsl:param name="projectName"/>
7	  <xsl:param name="keepPublishFirst" select="'true'"/>
8	
9	  <!-- Values the bundled /import data was exported with -->
10	  <xsl:variable name="applicationIdPlaceholder" select="'com.enonic.app.hmdb'"/>
11	  <xsl:variable name="projectNamePlaceholder" select="'hmdb'"/>
12	
13	  <xsl:variable name="applicationIdDashed" select="translate($applicationId, '.', '-')"/>
14	  <xsl:variable name="applicationIdPlaceholderDashed" select="translate($applicationIdPlaceholder, '.', '-')"/>
15	
16	  <!-- app key inside descriptor-style string values: "<app>:descriptor" -->
17	  <xsl:template match="string[starts-with(text(), concat($applicationIdPlaceholder, ':'))]">
18	    <string>
19	      <xsl:attribute name="name"><xsl:value-of select="@name"/></xsl:attribute>
20	      <xsl:value-of select="concat($applicationId, substring-after(., $applicationIdPlaceholder))"/>
21	    </string>
22	  </xsl:template>
23	
24	  <!-- bare app key string value -->
25	  <xsl:template match="string[text() = $applicationIdPlaceholder]">
26	    <string>
27	      <xsl:attribute name="name"><xsl:value-of select="@name"/></xsl:attribute>
28	      <xsl:value-of select="$applicationId"/>
29	    </string>
30	  </xsl:template>
31	
32	  <!-- dashed app key in property-set names (x.<dashed-app>...) -->
33	  <xsl:template match="property-set/@name[. = $applicationIdPlaceholderDashed]">
34	    <xsl:attribute name="name"><xsl:value-of select="$applicationIdDashed"/></xsl:attribute>
35	  </xsl:template>

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<xsl:stylesheet version="1.0" xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform">
  <xsl:output method="xml" indent="yes"/>

  <xsl:param name="applicationId"/>
  <xsl:param name="projectName"/>
  <xsl:param name="keepPublishFirst" select="'true'"/>

  <!-- Values the bundled /import data was exported with -->
  <xsl:variable name="applicationIdPlaceholder" select="'com.enonic.app.hmdb'"/>
  <xsl:variable name="projectNamePlaceholder" select="'hmdb'"/>

  <xsl:variable name="applicationIdDashed" select="translate($applicationId, '.', '-')"/>
  <xsl:variable name="applicationIdPlaceholderDashed" select="translate($applicationIdPlaceholder, '.', '-')"/>

  <!-- app key inside descriptor-style string values: "<app>:descriptor" -->
  <xsl:template match="string[starts-with(text(), concat($applicationIdPlaceholder, ':'))]">
    <string>
      <xsl:attribute name="name"><xsl:value-of select="@name"/></xsl:attribute>
      <xsl:value-of select="concat($applicationId, substring-after(., $applicationIdPlaceholder))"/>
    </string>
  </xsl:template>

  <!-- bare app key string value -->
  <xsl:template match="string[text() = $applicationIdPlaceholder]">
    <string>
      <xsl:attribute name="name"><xsl:value-of select="@name"/></xsl:attribute>
      <xsl:value-of select="$applicationId"/>
    </string>
  </xsl:template>

  <!-- dashed app key in property-set names (x.<dashed-app>...) -->
  <xsl:template match="property-set/@name[. = $applicationIdPlaceholderDashed]">
    <xsl:attribute name="name"><xsl:value-of select="$applicationIdDashed"/></xsl:attribute>
  </xsl:template>

  <!-- project-role principals: role:cms.project.<placeholder>.<suffix> -->
  <xsl:template match="principal/@key[starts-with(., concat('role:cms.project.', $projectNamePlaceholder, '.'))]">
    <xsl:attribute name="key">
      <xsl:value-of select="concat('role:cms.project.', $projectName, '.', substring-after(., concat('role:cms.project.', $projectNamePlaceholder, '.')))"/>
    </xsl:attribute>
  </xsl:template>

  <xsl:template match="@*|node()">
    <xsl:copy><xsl:apply-templates select="@*|node()"/></xsl:copy>
  </xsl:template>

  <!-- Remove publishing metadata on import -->
  <xsl:template match="data/property-set[@name='publish']">
    <xsl:if test="$keepPublishFirst != 'false'">
      <xsl:copy><xsl:apply-templates select="@*|*[@name='first']"/></xsl:copy>
    </xsl:if>
  </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>

14	export function GET(request: {
15	  params: { query?: string; start?: string; count?: string; ids?: string[] }
16	}) {
17	  const query = request.params.query || ""
18	  const start = parseInt(request.params.start || "0", 10)
19	  const count = parseInt(request.params.count || "10", 10)
20	
21	  try {
22	    const url = `${BACKEND_URL}/store/products?limit=${count}&offset=${start}` +
23	      (query ? `&q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}` : "")
24	
25	    const response = httpClient.request({
26	      url,
27	      method: "GET",
28	      headers: {
29	        "x-publishable-api-key": PUBLISHABLE_KEY,
30	      },
31	      contentType: "application/json",
32	    })
33	
34	    if (response.status !== 200) {
35	      throw new Error(`Medusa returned status ${response.status}`)
36	    }
37	
38	    const data = JSON.parse(response.body as string)
39	    const products: MedusaProduct[] = data.products || []
40	
41	    const hits = products.map((p) => ({
42	      id: p.handle,
43	      displayName: p.title,
44	      description: p.description || "",
45	      iconUrl: p.thumbnail || undefined,
46	    }))
47	
48	    return {
49	      status: 200,
50	      body: JSON.stringify({
51	        hits,
52	        count: hits.length,
53	        total: data.count || hits.length,
54	      }),
55	      contentType: "application/json",
56	    }
57	  } catch (e) {
58	    return {
59	      status: 500,
60	      body: JSON.stringify({ error: String(e) }),

62	    }

1	"use server"
2	
3	import { sdk } from "@lib/config"
4	import { sortProducts } from "@lib/util/sort-products"
5	import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/types"
6	import { SortOptions } from "@modules/store/components/refinement-list/sort-products"
7	import { getAuthHeaders, getCacheOptions } from "./cookies"
8	import { getRegion, retrieveRegion } from "./regions"
9	
10	export const listProducts = async ({
11	  pageParam = 1,
12	  queryParams,
13	  countryCode,
14	  regionId,
15	}: {
16	  pageParam?: number
17	  queryParams?: HttpTypes.FindParams & HttpTypes.StoreProductListParams
18	  countryCode?: string
19	  regionId?: string
20	}): Promise<{
21	  response: { products: HttpTypes.StoreProduct[]; count: number }
22	  nextPage: number | null
23	  queryParams?: HttpTypes.FindParams & HttpTypes.StoreProductListParams
24	}> => {
25	  if (!countryCode && !regionId) {
26	    throw new Error("Country code or region ID is required")
27	  }
28	
29	  const limit = queryParams?.limit || 12
30	  const _pageParam = Math.max(pageParam, 1)
31	  const offset = _pageParam === 1 ? 0 : (_pageParam - 1) * limit
32	
33	  let region: HttpTypes.StoreRegion | undefined | null
34	
35	  if (countryCode) {
36	    region = await getRegion(countryCode)
37	  } else {
38	    region = await retrieveRegion(regionId!)
39	  }
40	
41	  if (!region) {
42	    return {
43	      response: { products: [], count: 0 },
44	      nextPage: null,
45	    }
46	  }
47	
48	  const headers = {
49	    ...(await getAuthHeaders()),
50	  }
51	
52	  const next = {
53	    ...(await getCacheOptions("products")),
54	  }
55	
56	  return sdk.client
57	    .fetch<{ products: HttpTypes.StoreProduct[]; count: number }>(
58	      `/store/products`,
59	      {
60	        method: "GET",
61	        query: {
62	          limit,
63	          offset,
64	          region_id: region?.id,
65	          fields:
66	            "*variants.calculated_price,+variants.inventory_quantity,*variants.images,+metadata,+tags,",
67	          ...queryParams,
68	        },
69	        headers,
70	        next,
71	        cache: "force-cache",
72	      }
73	    )
74	    .then(({ products, count }) => {
75	      const nextPage = count > offset + limit ? pageParam + 1 : null
76	
77	      return {
78	        response: {
79	          products,
80	          count,
81	        },
82	        nextPage: nextPage,
83	        queryParams,
84	      }
85	    })
86	}
87	
88	/**
89	 * This will fetch 100 products to the Next.js cache and sort them based on the sortBy parameter.
90	 * It will then return the paginated products based on the page and limit parameters.
91	 */
92	export const listProductsWithSort = async ({
93	  page = 0,
94	  queryParams,
95	  sortBy = "created_at",
96	  countryCode,
97	}: {
98	  page?: number
99	  queryParams?: HttpTypes.FindParams & HttpTypes.StoreProductParams
100	  sortBy?: SortOptions
101	  countryCode: string
102	}): Promise<{
103	  response: { products: HttpTypes.StoreProduct[]; count: number }
104	  nextPage: number | null
105	  queryParams?: HttpTypes.FindParams & HttpTypes.StoreProductParams
106	}> => {
107	  const limit = queryParams?.limit || 12
108	
109	  const {
110	    response: { products, count },
111	  } = await listProducts({
112	    pageParam: 0,
113	    queryParams: {
114	      ...queryParams,
115	      limit: 100,
116	    },
117	    countryCode,
118	  })
119	
120	  const sortedProducts = sortProducts(products, sortBy)
121	
122	  const pageParam = (page - 1) * limit
123	
124	  const nextPage = count > pageParam + limit ? pageParam + limit : null
125	
126	  const paginatedProducts = sortedProducts.slice(pageParam, pageParam + limit)
127	
128	  return {
129	    response: {
130	      products: paginatedProducts,
131	      count,
132	    },
133	    nextPage,
134	    queryParams,
135	  }
136	}

Everything is working. Here's a complete summary of what was done:

---

## What was implemented

### Enonic App

**New descriptors:**
- `cms/pages/landing/landing.yaml` — Page descriptor with a single `main` region
- `cms/parts/product-showcase/product-showcase.yaml` — Part with `heading` (TextLine) and `products` (CustomSelector via `medusaProducts` service)

**Page template (both paths):**
- `import/hmdb/_templates/landing-page/_/node.xml` — Import data for fresh installs; template uses the `landing` page descriptor with `product-showcase` pre-placed in `main/0`, heading defaulting to "Featured Products"
- `lib/ensure-landing-page-template.ts` — Runtime bootstrap (runs at app startup) that creates the template on existing sandboxes using `contentLib.create()` + `nodeLib.modify()` to set the components. Template was created at `/home/_templates/landing-page` and pushed to master

**`main.ts`** — Calls `ensureLandingPageTemplate` as a startup task (alongside the existing `fixBrokenPageTemplates`)

**`site.yaml`** — Unchanged — the existing `preview.js` catch-all already handles `landing-page` content

### Frontend

- `src/components/enonic/pages/LandingPage.tsx` — Page component that renders `<RegionsView>` for the main region
- `src/components/enonic/parts/ProductShowcase.tsx` — Async server component that reads `part.config.products` (array of handles), fetches them from `/store/products?handle[]=...`, and renders a product grid with links to `/[countryCode]/products/[handle]`

message.content:
GOAL: Build a NEW, separate Product Detail Page as a genuine point of 
comparison against the existing one at /products/[handle]. This new PDP 
should be Enonic-composed (editor builds the page layout via parts in 
Content Studio), not a hardcoded React template like the current one.

CONTEXT: 
- enonic-app/ — Enonic XP8 app (com.enonic.app.hmdb)
- frontend/ — Next.js storefront
- Working custom selector: enonic-app/src/main/resources/services/medusaProducts/ 
  (Service, kind: Service, returns Medusa products for CustomSelector — 
  used by Collection's featuredProducts field, confirmed working)
- A Landing Page page/part/template system may have just been built in a 
  prior session (check cms/pages/, cms/parts/product-showcase/ if it 
  exists) — follow the SAME patterns/conventions for descriptors, 
  controllers, and site.yaml mappings as whatever was set up there, for 
  consistency. Do not duplicate effort — reuse the medusaProducts service 
  and any shared part-building conventions already established.
- IMPORTANT (confirmed via docs): there's no special "page-capable" 
  superType in XP — any content type can have a page assigned via Content 
  Studio's page editor / page templates. Don't add a "regions" section to 
  a content-type schema directly.

STEPS:

1. ENONIC — New content type: cms/content-types/product-page/product-page.yaml
   - superType: base:structured (same as other content types in this app)
   - Fields: 
     - "medusaHandle" (TextLine, required, min:1 max:1) — the Medusa 
       product handle this page represents, e.g. "sweatshirt"
     - Optionally a "heading" TextLine override field for editor-supplied 
       page title (falls back to Medusa product title if empty)

2. ENONIC — New part: cms/parts/product-detail/product-detail.yaml
   - This part has NO config fields of its own — it reads the medusaHandle 
     from its PARENT CONTENT (the product-page item it's placed on), not 
     from its own config. Check Enonic's part controller docs/conventions 
     for how a part accesses the containing content's data fields (likely 
     via portalLib.getContent() in the controller)
   - Controller (TypeScript): fetches nothing itself — the actual Medusa 
     fetch happens on the Next.js side; this part's controller is just for 
     the Content Studio EDITOR PREVIEW (can show a simple placeholder like 
     "Product: {medusaHandle}" using lib-thymeleaf or plain HTML, matching 
     the pattern in lib/preview.ts)

3. ENONIC — Page descriptor + page template
   - New page descriptor (cms/pages/product/product.yaml) with a single 
     region (e.g. "main")
   - New page template (provisioned same way as the Landing Page template 
     from the prior session) with the product-detail part PRE-PLACED in 
     the main region, so a new Product Page starts populated automatically

4. ENONIC — site.yaml mapping
   - Add a mapping for the product-page content type to render via this 
     page descriptor

5. FRONTEND — New route: frontend/src/app/[countryCode]/[...contentPath]/
   already exists and handles adapter-based content via MainView. Confirm 
   product-page content renders through it correctly at its real nested 
   path (e.g. /dk/home/sweatshirt-page or wherever it's created in the 
   content tree)

6. FRONTEND — "product-detail" part component
   - Map "product-detail" in src/components/_mappings.ts to a new React 
     component
   - This component receives the part's containing content data (the 
     medusaHandle field) — check how the adapter passes parent content 
     data to part view components (likely via props from MainView/
     ComponentRegistry, check existing _mappings.ts patterns or the 
     adapter's own docs/types)
   - Using medusaHandle, fetch the full product from Medusa (reuse 
     existing logic from src/lib/data/products.ts and the rendering 
     pieces from src/modules/products/templates/index.tsx — image gallery, 
     price, add-to-cart, etc. — adapt/reuse those components rather than 
     rewriting from scratch)
   - Render the full PDP experience using real Medusa data for whatever 
     handle the editor specified

VERIFY: Create a new Product Page content item under /home, set 
medusaHandle to "sweatshirt", confirm: (a) Content Studio shows it 
pre-populated with the product-detail part already placed, (b) it renders 
correctly on the Next.js frontend showing real Sweatshirt data (images, 
price, add-to-cart works), (c) it can be visually compared side-by-side 
with the existing /dk/products/sweatshirt page.

Do not break: /dk homepage, /dk/products, /dk/products/[handle] (existing 
PDP), /dk/collections/[handle], /dk/Blog/[slug], and whatever Landing Page 
system was built in the prior session.

content.content:
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project

Headless Movie DB (hmdb) — an Enonic XP sample/demonstration application (`com.enonic.app.hmdb`) that ships sample movie content and renders simple preview pages. Targets XP `8.0.0-SNAPSHOT` (see `gradle.properties`). Not a library/API-only app: it registers a site with controllers and content types, and auto-imports sample data on first install.

## Build & deploy

XP apps compile **through the connected sandbox**, not via the host JDK/Gradle. The Enonic CLI picks the sandbox from the `.enonic` file (gitignored) and the sandbox provides the JDK + Gradle runtime used for the build — don't debug build errors by inspecting local `java -version` or running `./gradlew` directly, and don't assume the host's Java matches what the build uses.

Primary commands:
- `enonic project build` — compile the app inside the connected sandbox.
- `enonic project deploy` — build and deploy the jar to the sandbox.
- `enonic project sandbox` — re-associate or switch the connected sandbox.

The `build.gradle` / `settings.gradle` files are authoritative for dependencies and plugins (`com.enonic.xp.app`, `com.enonic.xp.settings` from `settings.gradle`, and the `xplibs.*` version catalog), but the wrapper is invoked by the CLI against the sandbox runtime, so versions here must be compatible with what the sandbox ships — don't pin library versions inline; always go through `xplibs.*`.

The server code is **TypeScript**, compiled to `build/resources/main` by `tsdown` (config: `tsdown.config.ts`, one output `.js` per source file with the tree intact). Gradle drives npm via the `com.github.node-gradle.node` plugin: `npmBuild` (→ `jar`) runs `npm run build`, and `npmCheck` (→ `check`) runs `tsc --noEmit` + ESLint. `processResources` excludes `*.ts`/`*.tsx`/`*.json`/`.gitkeep` so only the compiled `.js` plus the copied descriptors land in the jar. You can run the toolchain directly (no sandbox needed) from the repo root: `npm install`, then `npm run check` / `npm run build`.

Type definitions come from `@enonic-types/*` (dev-only); `/lib/thymeleaf` types come from `@item-enonic-types/lib-thymeleaf`. No test framework is currently wired. The CI workflow (`.github/workflows/enonic-gradle.yml`) runs the shared `enonic/release-tools/build-and-publish` action.

## First-boot bootstrapping

`src/main/resources/main.ts` is the application entry point. On the cluster leader (`clusterLib.isLeader()`) it:

1. Runs in an admin context on repo `com.enonic.cms.hmdb`.
2. If the `hmdb` project does not exist, creates it via `lib-project` (`publicRead: true`, language `en`).
3. Imports `/import/hmdb` into `/content` using `exportLib.importNodes`, applying `import/replace_app.xsl` with `applicationId=app.name` so the exported XML references to the old app name are rewritten to the currently-deployed app on import.
4. Publishes `/hmdb` to `master`. In XP8 `contentLib.publish` takes no source/target branch — it publishes from the current context branch (`draft`, set in `runInContext`) to `master`, descendants included by default.

If you change `appName` in `gradle.properties` the XSLT substitution is what keeps imported content referring to the right app. Don't bypass it by hardcoding app IDs in the exported data.

## Resource layout (XP8)

Under `src/main/resources/`:

- `application.yaml` — top-level app manifest (`kind: "Application"`, title, description, vendor).
- `cms/` — all schemas the CMS cares about:
  - `site.yaml` — portal mappings (controllers matched by content type) and mounted Universal APIs (`apis:`, e.g. `asset`).
  - `cms.yaml` — app-level mixin bindings (which content types get which mixin fields).
  - `content-types/`, `pages/`, `parts/`, `layouts/`, `macros/`, `mixins/`, `styles/` — all YAML descriptors.
- `main.ts` — application entry point (see First-boot bootstrapping).
- `lib/` — portal controllers (TypeScript) registered via `cms/site.yaml` mappings:
  - `info.ts` — matches `type:'portal:site'`, plain HTML landing page.
  - `preview.ts` — matches `type:'(?!media:).*'` (every non-media type), uses `lib-thymeleaf` to render `preview.html` (a copied resource, not compiled).
- `i18n/` — translation bundles (`phrases.properties`, `phrases_no.properties`). Must live at `/i18n/`, not `/site/i18n/` (XP8 removed the site-scoped lookup).
- `assets/` — static assets (including `styles.css`). Served by `lib-asset`'s bundled **Asset API** (`assetUrl` is imported from `/lib/enonic/asset`, not `/lib/xp/portal`). The API ships inside the `lib-asset` jar; the app mounts it by listing `asset` under `apis:` in `cms/site.yaml` (XP8 Universal APIs are not exposed by default).
- `import/hmdb/` — XP content export used for first-boot bootstrapping, with `replace_app.xsl` rewriting app IDs on import.

Controllers are authored in TypeScript and compiled to `.js`, so the controller names in `cms/site.yaml` (e.g. `/lib/info.js`) are the **compiled** output paths. Use named uppercase HTTP-method exports — `export function GET(req)` / `POST` (compiled to `exports.GET`) — XP8 deprecated lowercase method names. A lowercase `all` export stays lowercase.

## Samples (not built)

`samples/review/` contains an example `review` content type XML and is **not** under `src/` — it's a copy-paste example for consumers of this demo, not part of the build. Leave it as a sample unless the user explicitly asks.

## Working conventions specific to XP apps

- Resources under `src/main/resources/` are served as classpath resources by XP; the `/lib/...` paths in controller `import` statements (and `resolve('...')` calls) are classpath-relative, not filesystem-relative. tsdown compiles the ESM `import`s to CommonJS and keeps the `/lib/xp/*` + `/lib/thymeleaf` references external (provided by the platform at runtime).
- Library deps in `build.gradle` use the `xplibs.*` catalog (e.g. `include xplibs.content`), not version-pinned coordinates. Third-party libs like `lib-thymeleaf` still use explicit coordinates.
- `include` vs `implementation` in `build.gradle`: `include` bundles the library inside the deployed app jar (used for `lib-xp:*` runtime libs and third-party `lib-*` deps), `implementation` is a compile-time-only XP API (e.g. `xplibs.api.script`). Keep that distinction when adding dependencies.
- Mixin bindings are split: mixin schemas live in `cms/mixins/<name>/<name>.yaml`, and the binding of "which content types get this mixin" lives in `cms/cms.yaml` under `mixins:` (with an `allowContentTypes` regex). Site mappings live separately in `cms/site.yaml`.

content.text:
Two phases: deploy the Enonic app, then create content and hit the frontend.

## 1. Deploy the Enonic app

From `enonic-app/`:
```
enonic project deploy
```

Watch the sandbox logs for these lines confirming the bootstrap ran:
```
[ensure-product-page-template] template already exists, skipping
```
(first deploy) or
```
[ensure-product-page-template] created template node: /content/hmdb/_templates/product-page
[ensure-product-page-template] pushed to master: success=1 failed=0
```

## 2. Create a Product Page content item in Content Studio

1. Open Content Studio at `http://localhost:8080/admin/tool/com.enonic.app.contentstudio/main`
2. Navigate into the **hmdb** project
3. Create new content → type **"Product Page"**
4. Fill in **Medusa Product Handle** with a real handle (e.g. `sweatshirt` — must exist in your Medusa instance)
5. The page template should auto-apply (you'll see the "Product Detail" placeholder box in the CS preview showing `Handle: sweatshirt`)
6. **Publish** the content item

## 3. Hit it in the frontend

Start the Next.js dev server if it isn't running:
```
cd frontend && npm run dev
```

Then visit:
```
http://localhost:3000/dk/<content-name>
```
where `<content-name>` is the `_name` slug Enonic assigned (shown in the content item's URL in CS, e.g. `sweatshirt` or `my-product-page`).

You should see the full Medusa `ProductTemplate` rendered — the same UI as `/dk/products/sweatshirt` but served through the Enonic composition layer.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| Template not created | Redeploy; check sandbox logs for `[ensure-product-page-template]` lines |
| CS preview shows "Component not found" | Verify `cms/parts/product-detail/product-detail.ts` compiled — rebuild with `enonic project deploy` |
| Frontend shows blank / PropsView | Check browser console; ensure `ENONIC_APP_NAME=com.enonic.app.hmdb` is set in `frontend/.env.local` |
| `notFound()` in ProductDetail | The handle doesn't match a Medusa product — double-check the handle string |
| Page template not applying | In CS, manually assign the "Product Page" template to the content item via the page editor |

content.content:
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project

Headless Movie DB (hmdb) — an Enonic XP sample/demonstration application (`com.enonic.app.hmdb`) that ships sample movie content and renders simple preview pages. Targets XP `8.0.0-SNAPSHOT` (see `gradle.properties`). Not a library/API-only app: it registers a site with controllers and content types, and auto-imports sample data on first install.

## Build & deploy

XP apps compile **through the connected sandbox**, not via the host JDK/Gradle. The Enonic CLI picks the sandbox from the `.enonic` file (gitignored) and the sandbox provides the JDK + Gradle runtime used for the build — don't debug build errors by inspecting local `java -version` or running `./gradlew` directly, and don't assume the host's Java matches what the build uses.

Primary commands:
- `enonic project build` — compile the app inside the connected sandbox.
- `enonic project deploy` — build and deploy the jar to the sandbox.
- `enonic project sandbox` — re-associate or switch the connected sandbox.

The `build.gradle` / `settings.gradle` files are authoritative for dependencies and plugins (`com.enonic.xp.app`, `com.enonic.xp.settings` from `settings.gradle`, and the `xplibs.*` version catalog), but the wrapper is invoked by the CLI against the sandbox runtime, so versions here must be compatible with what the sandbox ships — don't pin library versions inline; always go through `xplibs.*`.

The server code is **TypeScript**, compiled to `build/resources/main` by `tsdown` (config: `tsdown.config.ts`, one output `.js` per source file with the tree intact). Gradle drives npm via the `com.github.node-gradle.node` plugin: `npmBuild` (→ `jar`) runs `npm run build`, and `npmCheck` (→ `check`) runs `tsc --noEmit` + ESLint. `processResources` excludes `*.ts`/`*.tsx`/`*.json`/`.gitkeep` so only the compiled `.js` plus the copied descriptors land in the jar. You can run the toolchain directly (no sandbox needed) from the repo root: `npm install`, then `npm run check` / `npm run build`.

Type definitions come from `@enonic-types/*` (dev-only); `/lib/thymeleaf` types come from `@item-enonic-types/lib-thymeleaf`. No test framework is currently wired. The CI workflow (`.github/workflows/enonic-gradle.yml`) runs the shared `enonic/release-tools/build-and-publish` action.

## First-boot bootstrapping

`src/main/resources/main.ts` is the application entry point. On the cluster leader (`clusterLib.isLeader()`) it:

1. Runs in an admin context on repo `com.enonic.cms.hmdb`.
2. If the `hmdb` project does not exist, creates it via `lib-project` (`publicRead: true`, language `en`).
3. Imports `/import/hmdb` into `/content` using `exportLib.importNodes`, applying `import/replace_app.xsl` with `applicationId=app.name` so the exported XML references to the old app name are rewritten to the currently-deployed app on import.
4. Publishes `/hmdb` to `master`. In XP8 `contentLib.publish` takes no source/target branch — it publishes from the current context branch (`draft`, set in `runInContext`) to `master`, descendants included by default.

If you change `appName` in `gradle.properties` the XSLT substitution is what keeps imported content referring to the right app. Don't bypass it by hardcoding app IDs in the exported data.

## Resource layout (XP8)

Under `src/main/resources/`:

- `application.yaml` — top-level app manifest (`kind: "Application"`, title, description, vendor).
- `cms/` — all schemas the CMS cares about:
  - `site.yaml` — portal mappings (controllers matched by content type) and mounted Universal APIs (`apis:`, e.g. `asset`).
  - `cms.yaml` — app-level mixin bindings (which content types get which mixin fields).
  - `content-types/`, `pages/`, `parts/`, `layouts/`, `macros/`, `mixins/`, `styles/` — all YAML descriptors.
- `main.ts` — application entry point (see First-boot bootstrapping).
- `lib/` — portal controllers (TypeScript) registered via `cms/site.yaml` mappings:
  - `info.ts` — matches `type:'portal:site'`, plain HTML landing page.
  - `preview.ts` — matches `type:'(?!media:).*'` (every non-media type), uses `lib-thymeleaf` to render `preview.html` (a copied resource, not compiled).
- `i18n/` — translation bundles (`phrases.properties`, `phrases_no.properties`). Must live at `/i18n/`, not `/site/i18n/` (XP8 removed the site-scoped lookup).
- `assets/` — static assets (including `styles.css`). Served by `lib-asset`'s bundled **Asset API** (`assetUrl` is imported from `/lib/enonic/asset`, not `/lib/xp/portal`). The API ships inside the `lib-asset` jar; the app mounts it by listing `asset` under `apis:` in `cms/site.yaml` (XP8 Universal APIs are not exposed by default).
- `import/hmdb/` — XP content export used for first-boot bootstrapping, with `replace_app.xsl` rewriting app IDs on import.

Controllers are authored in TypeScript and compiled to `.js`, so the controller names in `cms/site.yaml` (e.g. `/lib/info.js`) are the **compiled** output paths. Use named uppercase HTTP-method exports — `export function GET(req)` / `POST` (compiled to `exports.GET`) — XP8 deprecated lowercase method names. A lowercase `all` export stays lowercase.

## Samples (not built)

`samples/review/` contains an example `review` content type XML and is **not** under `src/` — it's a copy-paste example for consumers of this demo, not part of the build. Leave it as a sample unless the user explicitly asks.

## Working conventions specific to XP apps

- Resources under `src/main/resources/` are served as classpath resources by XP; the `/lib/...` paths in controller `import` statements (and `resolve('...')` calls) are classpath-relative, not filesystem-relative. tsdown compiles the ESM `import`s to CommonJS and keeps the `/lib/xp/*` + `/lib/thymeleaf` references external (provided by the platform at runtime).
- Library deps in `build.gradle` use the `xplibs.*` catalog (e.g. `include xplibs.content`), not version-pinned coordinates. Third-party libs like `lib-thymeleaf` still use explicit coordinates.
- `include` vs `implementation` in `build.gradle`: `include` bundles the library inside the deployed app jar (used for `lib-xp:*` runtime libs and third-party `lib-*` deps), `implementation` is a compile-time-only XP API (e.g. `xplibs.api.script`). Keep that distinction when adding dependencies.
- Mixin bindings are split: mixin schemas live in `cms/mixins/<name>/<name>.yaml`, and the binding of "which content types get this mixin" lives in `cms/cms.yaml` under `mixins:` (with an `allowContentTypes` regex). Site mappings live separately in `cms/site.yaml`.

---
name: feedback-enonic-common-prop
description: The correct access path for dataAsJson in Enonic part components — common.get.dataAsJson, not common.guillotine.get.dataAsJson
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

In Enonic nextjs-adapter part components, `props.common` is the *unwrapped* guillotine result — the adapter calls `Object.values()` on the combined query response, stripping the `guillotine {}` wrapper.

**Correct:** `common?.get?.dataAsJson?.someField`  
**Wrong:** `common?.guillotine?.get?.dataAsJson?.someField`

**Why:** `fetchContentData` does `contents: Object.values(contentResults)` where `contentResults` is `{ request0: { get: {...}, getSite: {...} } }`. So `common` = `{ get: {...}, getSite: {...} }` — already inside the `guillotine {}` block.

**How to apply:** Any time a part component reads parent content data from `props.common`, use `common.get.dataAsJson` directly. The same applies to `common.get.displayName`, `common.get.type`, etc.
